verdict.label: duplicate
verdict.why: Both functions run the same provider-dispatch sequence. They resolve api_base and api_key from the provider config, with the ctx.api_key or litellm.api_key fallback. They then call base_llm_http_handler.completion with an identical argument mapping, and finally call logging.post_call with the same arguments and return the response. Only the config class (EdenAIChatConfig vs FalAIChatConfig) and the custom_llm_provider string differ. fal_ai also adds a streaming-rejection guard up front, which can stay in its caller. A shared helper such as _dispatch_base_http_completion(ctx, provider_name, config_cls, pre_validate=None) would own the common sequence, and each provider function would stay a thin adapter. This is the same executable policy repeated, not just a shared helper call: it composes config resolution, handler invocation and post-call logging. If other providers repeat it too, the case for extraction is stronger.
